rcmp_principle: The theoretical prediction, the observable, and the measurement instrument must all be defined within, or have explicit and derived mappings between, the same regime(s).

architectures.name: Pure L2 (galactic interior)
architectures.observable: d log(g_obs/g_bar) / d log g_bar at 1e-2 < g_bar/a_0 < 1e-1
architectures.prediction: D_eff modifies the shape of the RAR in the deep-MOND regime, not just its value at a_0. If environmental density modulates D_eff, the RAR slope at g/a_0 ~ 0.01-0.1 should correlate with environment.
architectures.why_it_works: Measurement point is far from the regime boundary. Unlike R(a_0), the deep-MOND slope probes a regime where the response function has saturated (mu >> 1), reducing sensitivity to boundary fluctuations and isolating the intrinsic L2 dynamics. The RAR slope in deep MOND is a stable L2 quantity with lower intrinsic scatter than R at a_0, and is directly sensitive to the functional form of D_eff rather than its value at a single point.

architectures.name: Pure L1 (cosmological growth)
architectures.observable: fsigma8(z) from redshift-space distortions, or void-cluster growth rate comparison
architectures.prediction: D_eff enters the cosmological background through Gamma(rho), which controls the growth rate fsigma8(z). Environmental density at L1 scales directly modulates Gamma without cross-regime coupling.
architectures.data_source: BOSS DR12, eBOSS DR16, DESI DR1 fsigma8; void-cluster catalogues
architectures.why_it_works: Everything is in L1. The MCMC inference pipeline already constrains alpha_L1.

architectures.name: Derived L1->L2 mapping
architectures.observable: same as KT3b, but with predicted alpha(k, z) rather than free parameter
architectures.prediction: Derive alpha from the EFC action by computing how the background S-field at L1 scales enters the boundary conditions of the L2 Poisson equation.
architectures.why_it_is_hard: Requires solving the coupled (g_mu_nu, S) system across scales, which is an open problem in EFC.
